title: Ruin, unnamed on the 1:25 000
summary: Four walls to shoulder height, a hearth, an ash tree growing where the door was.

place.name: Head of the cwm, above Llyn Idwal

body.text: The map marks it, as it marks all such things, with the word sheepfold, which it is not.

The walls are drystone, roughly a metre thick, with through-stones still in place. There is a lintelled opening on the south-east side and a hearth in the north wall with the back stones fire-reddened to a depth of about thirty millimetres. Sheepfolds do not have hearths.

It is almost certainly a hafod: summer accommodation, occupied for perhaps ten weeks a year while stock were on the high grazing, abandoned by the middle of the nineteenth century when the practice stopped being worth the walk.
The ash is about forty years old and is directly in the doorway, which is a thing ash trees seem to enjoy doing.
Coordinates are recorded to a precision the archive considers appropriate rather than to the precision available.

footnotes.text: Ordnance Survey uses a small number of generic labels for unidentified rural structures. This is sensible cartography and occasionally poor history.
